[b]| EXTRA |[/b] [u][i]Years in Review: Lernei Sammite's Government[/i][/u] [b]| EXTRA |[/b]
[i]What has the president achieved since his rise in 2023?[/i]
[sub][i]Erene RP[/i][/sub]]
In a landmark election in 2023, Banhockia chose to end the stewardship of the longstanding [i]Advance, Banhockia![/i] (AB!) party after thirty years of rule, having controlled the legislature since the governmental crisis of 1992, and the executive since 1998. Taking the throne following the ballot was a relatively unknown figure in national politics yet always a loyal, standout member of the newly elected party, the [i]CGT[/i]. Lernei Sammite, hailing from Enmanhol, would be removing the popular however cautious Habel Samaba, who'd shown restraint in backing her own coalition in the election, emphasized by her choice not to run for a second term.

In fact, the increasing tensions in AB! were poorly hidden by the party's authorities. By 2022, with a crucial year in office for Habel coming, her party's hold on the Junior Directory, already falling apart since the beginning of her tenure, could not hold their majority together due to infighting relating to tax cuts and an embezzlement scandal in the middle of the cycle. This caused the friendly upper chamber that the verticists (a Banhock political ideology) had managed to cultivate to collapse in a similar fashion. Habel was too beloved to find herself as the main casualty of the destruction of her surroundings, but she certainly took a hit, and soon, her long-anticipated reign, already doubted by a large segment of the populace, seemed like a term that AB! was going to have to damage control in. This was overdue, even for the president herself. She detailed in an interview in 2026 that, knowing her already elevated stature nationwide, [i]Advance, Banhockia![/i] likely selected her to assure another term for them in the executive, even with their diminishing parliamentary majorities.

The election itself, in hindsight, has become a topic of debate among those in the political sphere, portraying the CGT's victory not so much as their own win, but more of an AB! defeat. Some viewed the now-ruling party's sizable 7-seat gain through a lens that saw AB!'s voter-attraction tactics as 'fearmongering' and 'unmotivating', a characteristic in their advertisement policy since the beginning of their dominance. Primarily, this is believed to have eliminated the threat of the today-defunct NAP; but also extends to the CGT, since 2023 was the only time it won an election, possibly as a result of this apparent campaign. Another factor which proves this is the rise of the [i]Union 45[/i] movement, introducing itself as the first, unified, major third party in more than 60 years, splitting much of the vote with AB! and bringing worries to the party of being the next NAP. Nonetheless, Lernei cruised to 49.8% of the vote, 13 points above AB! candidate Hurii Ghelonaa, and he was ready to bring major changes to Banhock politics.

As soon as Lernei's administration began, welcomed by thousands hoping for a radical shifts in government operations, in particular concerning corruption, there was movement. Immediately, with a month to do it, the CGT set out to create a budget for the fiscal year which would turn the AB!'s previous bills on their heads. At first, the 2023 funding bill sought to: unify social welfare benefits into a single system; finance infrastructure more than any other sector; divert certain ministries' funding to scientific endeavors; and more. However, likely due to the first condition, it was rejected by the Senior Directory (upper chamber), which got flamed by the president, who pressured it to approve the plan on its second try, with some minimal edits. The new budget was also readily focused on bringing down unemployment, a rising issue in the last few years.

In a similar vein, Lernei's government intended to stave off from further international influence and trade, a defining attribute of Habel's government. However, wanting to prevent inflation while also defeating unemployment, the budgetary bill also allocated some funds to the purchase of approximately 𝔽'855 million ($15 million) in foreign reserves, looking to stabilize the Flor in the wake of incrementing debts, to later implement isolationist policies without the worries of international pressure. Separately, the ADD (Transliterated abbreviation of funding bills) elaborated on the creation of Dalerha, the overseas territory in Kianzhou, long in the plans of AB! administrations. Before the election, it was suspected that the CGT would defund the project, which was also seen as a stunt by the former government to gain popularity ahead of the 2013 ballot. However, Lernei quickly put down those expectations, as he said after the bill's approval: "The time and effort the government has spent on [Dalerha], it's too much to waste. The opportunities, in any case, are endless, and we will abuse them. Unlike previous administrations, we do not stop in the middle of the path. We will continue; and the territory will be greater than anything previously anticipated."

Even so, the official foundation of Dalerha wouldn't be announced until the next year, with the second ADD under his reign. Within that year into his rule, however, Lernei encountered an increasingly unfriendly Senior Directory, since it only permitted the passage of 62 relatively minor reforms within the same timeframe. The bigger packages were routinely rejected; including the investment into a wind farm in southern Taakarsu island, renovations to facilities in mining villages on both sides of Marmella, and importantly, his long-awaited "refitting" acts, a central part of his campaign and aimed at eliminating or drastically altering laws of the Emmelei administration (1996-2003). Lernei primarily intended to devolve much tax and subsidization power to local governments, however, the upper chamber voiced concerns in relation to how the proposals were more likely to eventually impoverish than enrich; especially because of certain elements which could've possibly hurt the local tourism sector.

Because of the souring relationship, Lernei's government was entering its second year with a legislature the president himself denominated 'toothless', and its popularity was already waning. While economic output rose in every quarter that he'd been in government, so did inflation and a rise in poverty. Nonetheless, the first year was quite uneventful, until May, when companies were completely allowed to set up operations in Dalerha, although with only 27% of the territory's lands being dedicated to private property, and a maximum workforce of 8 per square kilometer. Analysts, while noticing the jubilation among the populace, hoping to see Dalerha be as prosperous as purported, detailed how Lernei was seemingly trying to cut his losses by limiting the project in so many ways. Additionally, the government invested just around 𝔽'1.1 billion ($20.5 million) into state-owned facilities, but also desiring to reinvest anything earned back into the area, particularly in its possible copper and gold reserves. The same measure would try to tap into the tiny island of Pohibo's coal mines.

For these actions, however, Lernei wasn't entirely revered. Much of his platform was on the basis of advancing with science-oriented projects, such as renewable energy. Though, as he discovered in the contemporary Parliament, it wasn't going to be easy to execute, and as such, dedicated some time to otherwise uncharacteristic acts. In no time, despite jobs appearing due to Dalerha and a bonuses program which was instituted nationwide, inflation soared to 11.2% in July alone, with 18.5% YOY. Protests in Enmanhol led to the resignation of the city's Port Overseer, while those in Masaega turned violent after police retribution against a drug trafficker spread to bystanders, almost ending with the burning of the local station. The bad PR was only momentary, as things stabilized in August, and Lernei pressured Masaega Chief Redi Ogaiga Huemat to step down. However, with sinking approval ratings and looming Senior Directory elections, the president was forced to act fast.

With two months left, Lernei utilized a tool often disregarded in Banhock politics. The Senior Directory is, by law, entirely made up of independents. Political parties are prohibited from funding campaigns in these votes in which the 14 electable members of the chamber are selected and therefore remain quite inactive in this period, even if there are obvious benefits depending on the results. In spite of these conditions, the CGT instituted an ad campaign on national television, in which Lernei himself appeared, to openly oppose the current make-up of the chamber and, quote: "Observe and go to the horizon", in reference to the political orientation held by the president. Public outcry was immediate, especially from opposition parties, which sought legal action against the administration for infringement of longstanding political norms. However, in the wake of the controversy, courts denied taking the CGT to trial, stating that, unless there was a direct connection between the participating candidates and the coalition (which hasn't been found as of yet), the third party cannot be prosecuted.

It is believed that this, alongside the already radioactive relationship between the concurrent Directory and President, was manifested in the huge gains the horizonists made in the election, bolstered by perceived political unity (a quality lacking in the verticist space) and a desire to progress with the ongoing plans of Lernei's government.

Now that the horizonists (unofficially) controlled the entire legislature, alongside the presidency if such intervention was required, the Lernei administration finally got to work on its highest priorities. Alongside the fact he now saw greater poll numbers, it was the strongest he'd been throughout his entire time in government. As such, reforms previously postponed were going into effect quickly, with a reported average of 8 bills passed per day. This included the aforementioned tax changes, which added some new statutes which kept the system relatively in the hands of the central government. Additionally, utilizing the pressure from the Masaega police scandal, Lernei also managed to centralize law enforcement and, in the process, put restrictions on private services. These actions attracted accusations of manipulation of the establishment and as being democracy-threatening. The overhaul was proving popular with some segments of the populace, however.

Social conservatives, an ever-decreasing sector of people, were elated by the end of calls to establish more public holidays and also celebrated the nationalization of certain institutes such as that of the Banhega language. Similarly, however, worries from the other end of the spectrum loosened, since citizenship laws, just like tariffs, home ownership and marriage codes were mostly left alone. This contributed to the picturing of Lernei as appealing to either side of the aisle. Though, some of his bigger scandals were yet to arrive.

In Dalerha, two young men were killed by an explosion at a government chemicals facility, with the reactive products having been labeled as 'necessary for mining' but had no extra equipment in the vicinity to prevent any disaster from occurring. This resulted in backlash over the security of determined regions, an issue which was blamed on the redistribution of legal and health programs and duties, which took away much responsibility but also autonomy from lesser-surveilled areas. In a separate case, following the revoking of media rights for several corporations (not actual networks, rather companies which do business through them, including hosting programs), Lernei had many feuds with public entertainment figures on how the justification was valid, despite the vague explanations received by most of the damaged corporations. The latter situation hurt his connection with residents of smaller islands, as Lernei built much of his own platform on the federalization of many elements of the society.

Other acts which made headlines, excluding those of tax rules (since these were very tenuous, though the expected revenue remained mostly unchanged), were the application of subsidies to trade schools while halving the education ministry's budget; the approval of a 𝔽'1.54 billion ($27 million) hydro power station in northern Marmella, raising concerns of unfair treatment of renewables in the rest of the country; and comments the president made on changing the legal order of election of the legislature, after a group of its unelected members prevented the sanctioning of a judge who dismissed a major land-ownership case between the state and a foreign-born farmer.

However, overall, it seems that there is still a group that is unimpressed. While the make-up of political discussion in Banhockia limits enormous shifts in the management of properties, international relations, etc., a large subsect of citizens feel disillusioned with the government for one reason: it's not doing enough. Polls find that not only has the CGT conceded its giant lead and only leads AB! by a few percentage points, but even 1 in 5 of its presumed voters view Lernei as 'contradictory' and see his administration as holding back too much. These issues, expressly arising for the first time during his tenure, might be a vestige of Banhock politics, and the way Lernei will address them, being the first of his kind to do so in years, will be interesting. It's possible that many view his tactics as badly as the opposition does, even if it's through the same reasoning as his own. 'Hypothetical' and 'out of touch', words which resonate among many throughout the entire spectrum, and as horizonism and verticism would have you believe, simply the fate of electoral politics. Unified in hatred, and unknowingly, ideals.
[/spoiler]

[b]August 2nd, 2027[/b]
[b][i]Broadcast - Meritavan News Channels[/i][/b]

Today, the Tsardom of Meritava officially began a transformation period in the leadership of Tsar Aleksandr I Meritavsky, who succeeded the previous ruler in peace. The Tsar delivered a vision of a modern, disciplined and strategically prepared Meritava in a national televised address, marking the end of decades of isolation. Once more shall Meritava address the world, The Tsar said. [i]"Not out of feebleness, but of vision and power. Isolation failed to save us; it will be preparation and determination."[/i]

To restore the relations with foreign states, Meritava declared the re-opening of its diplomatic missions and restoring ties with the neighbouring states and the region. The long closed embassies and consulates are being reopened and the government is inviting its friendly countries to join in collective research and industrial ventures as well as in sharing of culture. Concurrently, foreign investment programmes managed by the states are also being initiated, which enables strategic alliances in infrastructure, energy, and technology without interfering with the sovereignty of the nation. The Tsar also stressed that the interaction of Meritava with the world will be reasonable, disciplined and respectful to its independence. responsible will we be, he said. [i]"Show respect to Meritava and you will find a partner. Judge us wrong, And you will see our determination."[/i]

At the domestic level, the Tsar has launched an all-encompassing bundle of legal and social reforms which will not only modernize Meritava but also concentrate the state power. Civil rights have been broadened: homosexuality has been legalized and the relationships between people made private, the laws regulating marriage have been revised so that civil and religious marriage are treated equally, gender equality has become a necessity in all state institutions. The young generation has been better equipped with education to a point of eighteen years and the public healthcare has been made universally accessible. Meanwhile, unwarranted abortions have been outlawed, and there is now a tight control on the provision of medical exemptions, and state welfare programmes of the elderly and the poor have been extended to offer social security.

These social reforms have accompanied political power. The protests and demonstrations which were not authorized are now forbidden, the political activity is limited to the state approved organizations. There are massive reforms in the civil service which has brought in meritocracy in recruiting and strengthened technocratic governance. The local governments have been centralized into the hands of the central government and its committees have been set up to check on major economic, scientific and military projects. These reforms are set to give Meritava the stability and efficiency it needs in the execution of its radical modernization agenda.

On the economic front, the Tsar has revealed a set of state run projects aimed at modernizing the industry and infrastructure on the one hand, and securing the availability of resources on the other. The welcome to foreign investments is being conditional and strictly restricted so that they can benefit the national interests. Significant infrastructure is being developed to enhance transportation, build urban centers that can support the population in extreme climatic systems, and upgrade the logistics routes in the North. Some resource management laws have also been changed to help the need of the strategic minerals such as oil, lithium, aluminium, and gold and industrial programmes have been initiated to incentivize state-led as well as privatized enterprise. There are also trade and customs reforms which have been undertaken to enable safe and efficient international trade.

The same has been applied to scientific and military programmes. Although currently Meritava is not using weapons of mass destruction, the Tsar has legalized and given importance to nuclear research with state supervision with civilian energy production and technological advancement being the priorities. There is also military modernization efforts underway in the air, naval and missile and radar systems and there has been an expansion of strategic reserves to make countries more resilient and be able to launch quick response. Such programmes are enriched by the establishment of the research centers devoted to the aerospace, energy, and industrial technology, and with the help of them, Meritava will also be on the leading positions in terms of strategic innovations.

The Tsar has stressed on the value of the Merkavian heritage and identity, which is culturally inclined. National holidays commemorating the history of the nation have been restored and state support of the arts, literature as well as historical preservation is increased. There has been the codification of religious tolerance, whereby the recognized faiths are under the supervision of the government. In such ways, Meritava aims at building a disciplined yet proud society of its cultural heritage and is open to the contemporary ideas and technologies.

At the end of his speech, Tsar Aleksandr I stated that Meritava is going into a period of power, peace, and vision. He said that Meritava would protect its citizens, promote its wisdom, and interact with the world in its own manner. Observers state that Meritava is placing itself as a centralized, technologically advanced, and authority regional power, and is prepared to come out of the decades of isolation. the days of isolation have passed, and Meritava is now open to the world, ready to the difficulties of the future, and bent on making herself felt as a sovereign state, with discipline and foresight.
